2025-12-02]  I'm designing a jungle gym / climbable shelf structure for the play area of our home. The sofa-like structure to the left is folding mattress you can slide under the monkey bars. If you've ever build something similar I'd be happy to take advice
2025-11-19]  I think it gives a pretty good sense of a dynamic ocean without being too distractive
2025-11-19]  It's based on a looping vertex shader. The data is baked at generation-time. Each vert has an in-direction, an out-direction and a time offset.
2025-11-19]  Got some pretty sweet new shore waves going
2025-03-05]  Yet another hallway design
2025-02-13]  Further iterations on hallway design
2024-11-01]  A fluffy cloud shader. It is using the same impostors as the trees, in case that isn't obvious.

2024-10-25]  Here, the shoreline is shown in yellow. A pushed out and smoothed shoreline is shown in blue. The waves travel from the blue line to the yellow (and back a little). There is also a global water mask texture that adds extra foam around rocks and stuff.

2024-10-25]  Shoreline waves! This is something I've tackled many times. Although this one is very subtle, it's my favorite thus far. Instead of trying to make the waves roll in and out inside one shader pass, I'm creating loads of overlapping waves that each go through their own cycle

2024-10-24]  Made some octagonal impostors for these trees. Might seem like overkill for such a stylized look, but they're a lot more stable when rotating the camera than all other billboard solutions I've tried, which is kinda important.
2024-05-29]  I'm putting together a navigation structure that lets you travel faster along rivers (and especially downstream)
2024-05-16]  Trying out a new lighting solution. This one is just one lookup in the vertex shader of a low res cube map height map.
2024-05-02]  Mountain textures! These have been tricky. Mountains kinda need lighting and normals, but with my texture blending tech I don't think I can afford that on low-end devices
2024-04-26]  Texture test!

2024-04-19]  Ok this might not look like much but I've got seamless patch blending! Some of the patches are projected (like the grass and the water) and some are manually UV-mapped (like the shoreline). With some good textures and some height based blending this is gonna be great.

2024-03-18]  Mega river system! I've had trouble making good rivers before. Now I've sort of special cased the rivers by collapsing them depth-first to let them wiggle real far, and then the rest is collapsed breadth-first, making nice gentle slopes that only occasionally meet steep cliffs.

2024-03-18]  In cute tile based planets like this you often get a "mushrooming" issue where tall mountains get weirdly wide. I managed to mitigate this by a relax pass where all module-containing cells try to achieve their desired shape and size. Note the cells on the top left contracting.
2024-03-15]  For reasons I will not be explaining at this point I've gone and put this on a sphere
2024-03-05]  Here, I'm visualizing the recursive tree parsing as it adds new rects. Note that when the board is more fragmented the arm tends to have more fingers.

2024-03-05]  Now supports removing rects too! The bin space gets quite fragmented after a while though.. I've tried to optimize it on the fly but I can't figure out how to when it get sort of interlocked. Still packs tight though!

2024-03-05]  A cute binary tree rect packer. Generating the placement attempts is kinda brute force (to get into all the nooks and crannies), but then it's using the tree properly for fast collision checks. I think this is the first time I've actually written a proper space partion tree. Fun.
2024-02-15]  It's simply a stack of planes sampling an SDF I had laying around. Gives a much more fluid vibe than the basic flipped mesh approach in Bad North and Townscaper
2024-02-15]  New water reflection I'm quite happy with

2024-01-29]  Some nice new highlights when the island is backlit. Achieved by simply adding another inverted mesh outline layer that shows up when looking into the sun. And masked by shadows, of course.

2024-01-29]  I can now force specific modules to appear. To do this I first generate the specific bit of grid they need. A large module like this would be highly unlikely to appear by chance on a random grid.

2023-11-14]  Ok, here's a small example. The button toggles a ScriptableObject bool. The FloatSelectNode component listens to that ScriptableObject, and then a series of node-like components end up moving a piece of UI

2023-10-18]  Another strange texturing style. This time trying to look a bit like abstract fields. A nice thing is they show the game tiles quite clearly. In the end I probably want a mix where some areas are more man made and others more natural.
2023-10-11]  Another take on a palette authoring tool
2023-10-05]  Ok here's a probably horrible way to author color volumes. The idea is to properly define the whole color possibility space for each feature
2023-10-02]  a cool cliff I came across
2023-09-28]  And here's a couple more being generated

2023-09-28]  They are of course 100% texture, painted onto a fairly low, poly mesh. I keep thinking I'm gonna need to give em some volume with billboard sprites, but now I'm not so sure anymore. Especially with the lil' shadows, they look quite volumetric as they are.
2023-09-28]  I added back the lil' shrubbery at the edges of things for like the 3rd time

2023-09-22]  I tamed the texture based surface shadows a bit, so the shadow casting height is independent of the z test height. Now I only get shadows over grass-cliff edges and under roofs. It has some artifacts across UV borders, but it's quite subtle so I might not actually have to fix it.

2023-09-19]  Ok, I think maybe this is a bit of a sweet spot. It's got a nice variable density texture to it. There are some height segmentation lines to help with readability, but they don't feel too synthetic.

2023-09-19]  I tried some texture based shadows. Note the shadows on the grass and along the roof edges. Looks kinda cool, but feels a bit too 3D for what I'm going for this time. I feel like it clashes with lines, and I like lines more.
2023-09-18]  Looking at my procedural stylized ground texturing again. Really like the swirly blobbyness of these. They feel kind of damp for some reason.

2023-09-05]  Oh! And now I finally figured out how to make non-straight sedimentary lines! Most of the texturing math is kinda linear, so I though the lines had to be linear too. But I could (obviously) just make the whole world wobbly, do the texturing math, then simply undo the wobble.
2023-09-05]  Looking att sedimentation lines again. Helps make large cliffs more interesting. Also makes their shape a bit more readable maybe.
2023-08-30]  On the other hand, I've always wanted to make a game in the Art Nouveau style. This might be a good fit. Look how neat and controlled the grass blotches bleed over the cliff edges.

2023-08-30]  I'm slowly emerging from a huge refactoring... While this here is not exactly the look I'm going for, it's showing off a big improvement to the texturing. I'm now able to draw with much bigger blotches without the blotches bleeding across and messing up important edges.

2023-07-07]  I am (once again) rewriting my generic triangle graph system to (hopefully) be more robust and generic. Here's a stress test where I'm adding random verts, making sure the graph stays mainifold and delauney-ish along the way.
2023-06-22]  Hmm.. I thought it was gonna be too wacky but maybe it's kinda cool
2023-06-22]  If your terrain generator supports overhangs you gotta flaunt it. I don't make the rules, but I do follow them.

2023-06-19]  Oh, and I finally got this lovely rock feature to show up! When working with WFC, sometimes you build a cool tile and it wont show up in forever, since it's conditions are so specific. You forget about it, and then suddenly: poof!
2023-06-19]  I'm prepping for a talk in Cambridge next week, thus all the gifs. I made my generator also output pure triangle/hex and square grids, to illustrate why I'm going for my mixed approach.

2023-06-19]  Here's a comparison showing no-, dumb- and hierarchical smoothing. The hierarchical smoothing helps preserve the intent of the input-tiles while smoothing out the jankyness from the weird underlying grid and from the limited slope angles in the input tileset

2023-06-19]  I smooth my mesh according to an edge type hierarchy. Black is hard, red is game-tile-border and blue is material-border. Verts only get to pull at equal or lower order verts, and only along the appropriate edges

2023-06-17]  I figured out how to mimic Thread.Sleep() in Burst! Just store time in a static unsafe NativeArray! Then you can write to it from the main thread and read from it inside a job! Probably super bad in many ways but good enough for visualization and debug!
2023-06-15]  The generator consistently spits out pretty cool islands now

2023-06-07]  I've been banging my head against various shore line rendering options for a good week now. Gonna stick with this for now I think, which is basically just a refined version of what I did for Bad North and Townscaper.

2023-06-02]  Here's a distance field-like mesh skirt solution very similar to Townscaper and Bad North. It works for calm waters I guess... But I would like something with a bit more punch this time. A bit more crashing waves.

2023-06-02]  I'm trying out using a shader based fluid simulation. But I'm skeptical. It seems to need 32 bit float render targets, and I don't trust that those will work across platforms. Might also be a challenge to tweak, stylize, and feed back to CPU if needed.
2023-05-05]  An quaint island being procedurally generated

2022-11-17]  Making a lil dynamic sprite packer, able to add and remove sprite allotments at runtime. I had one of these in Bad North and found it very useful. Here, the sprites are baked live from meshes. So I guess it's basically impostors. Though I expect to use it for much else too.

2022-11-10]  In the vertex shader, my grass gets to sample that contrast texture both where they stand, and also raycast into the background. The outline strength is determined by the difference between these two samples! Not perfect, but pretty good! Not too jittery when turning the camera
2022-11-10]  An early look at grass billboards. I really like how they add a completely new kind of shape and detail frequency.

2022-10-24]  I wrote a thing to splice houses into the terrain. Mostly, the houses are part of pre-build tiles, but would be useful insert them at will too. You can kinda see the structure of my mesh system and mesh algoritms by how the yellow lines are rotating around the verts.

2022-10-19]  I'm seeing if my light volume approach can work with point lights too. The low resolution is noticeable for sure. Especially when you move em around like this. But if you keep em big and soft and somewhat still I think it's gonna be good.

2022-10-18]  I thought it would be too expensive to properly evaluate each tile placement. But! While the number of possible tiles is indeed very large, it is actually quite small around the collapsed edge! Thus, my algorithm now tries to expand (and interconnect) a simplified nav graph.

2022-10-14]  Here's the slowed down bounce sequence. You can see how the mega texture and the light volume affect each other back and forth. After about the 3rd bounce, further bounces are not noticeable.

2022-10-14]  1st texture here is an sdf volume. The distance lives in the alpha, but RG actually reference UVs in the mega texture! 2nd is a baked 6 directional light volume, raycast against the sdf, sampling the mega texture using the UVs where it hits the sdf. 3rd is the lit mega texture

2022-10-14]  I always write my own lighting solutions. I've had some really naive ad hoc color bleeding in my (very fake) GI before, but this is my first decent attempt to actually have the light *bounce*

2022-10-12]  I start with a very basic Marching Cubes mesh from a bunch of spheres. I mark the edges between triangles that are closest to different spheres. Then I run an iterative relax algorithm where those hard edges are like rubber bands, and the rest is sort of a like a balloon.
2022-10-12]  Can you make good looking foliage from Marching Cubes-blobs? Maybe?

2022-10-10]  Obviously, it's all tile-based. I went through a major rewrite to combine an irregular grid (like in Townscaper) with multi-cell tiles (like in Bad North). Note how one of the house tiles even cover both a square tile AND a triangular tile
2022-10-10]  To make the cliffs look more organic, I'm doing some pretty radical cage deformation on the cells.
2022-10-10]  I'm back on the island generation
2022-02-05]  Late night cryptic graph tweet

2022-01-15]  I created a dedicated contrast texture system for the lines: an iterative simulation on the triangles that starts random and then tries to make contrasted edges different, and non-contrasted edges similar. A byproduct is a beautiful color gradient that help express connectivity

2022-01-14]  Ok, I stumbled on a pretty cool art style now. Here, I'm creating pixel thin lines from contrasts in my procedural normal map. I should probably move to a bespoke contrast texture (to get more deliberate control over the lines). But I gotta say this looks pretty promising.

2022-01-13]  Yet another light baker. Actually does some ray marching, but still pretty ad hoc. The textures are: 1. Normals (procedurally painted in big chunky strokes) 2. 3D Signed Distance Field 3. 3D Ambient Occlusion in positive and negative X,Y and Z

2022-01-10]  More experiments in procedural texturing of procedural islands. Still very early, but I do like these big paint blotches. They hide the polys well and they would be hard to achieve with other means. Definitely need a proper lighting system though. And probably some outlines.

2022-01-03]  Yeah that's good enough for now. I quite like how the radial (instead of directional) size-sorting looks. Gonna make for some visually pleasing textures with that big coherent chunk in the middle.

2020-12-15]  Apparently, one way to do Delaunay Triangulation on a sphere is to do it on a Stereographic Projection. (Many people have done this before me, so it's nothing new). My points are sorted vertically, which means radially, which makes the algorithm faster. Here's what it looks like:

2020-12-15]  Apropos of nothing, a take on the ancient issue of generating nice triangulated spheres 1. Random points 2. Space out the points 3. Triangulate 4. Relax using the triangles Unclear if I'll use this for anything helpful sources: https:// redblobgames.com/x/1842-delauna y-voronoi-sphere/ … https:// newcastle.edu.au/__data/assets/ pdf_file/0017/22508/13_A-fast-algorithm-for-constructing-Delaunay-triangulations-in-the-plane.pdf …

2020-11-27]  How the infinite grid is relaxed and kept seamless: The grid is made of Patches. Adjacent triplets form Clusters. Clusters and Patches are relaxed independently. Each Vert is a triangular interpolation its representation in the closest 2 Clusters and the Patch wherein it sits.

2020-11-26]  Townscaper now has lighthouses! This pattern required more code rewrite than seems reasonable. Luckily, I got some slight optimization out of it too. https:// store.steampowered.com/app/1291340/To wnscaper/ …

2020-09-28]  Ok, I tried the mixed perspective. Note how houses further away are smaller, yet the vertical lines stay straight and parallel. It's definitely not a good fit for Townscaper, but might work well if I make another Bad North-ish game with a hearty mix of 3D meshes and billboards.

2020-09-15]  To soften it up a bit, I'm trying out a penumbra approach where I draw the shadow thrice, once normal, once pulled in slightly and once with big voxels. I think I like it. (here, the shadow is shown darker than it should be to demonstrate the effect)

2020-09-15]  I'm exploring cast shadows. They have to be quite subtle and soft to fit the style. It does seems like they should be fast enough for mobile too if I only update them on command after a regeneration.
